name: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Headache Society Diagnostic Criteria for Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome

criteria.description: Unilateral orbital pain persisting for weeks if untreated
Paresis of one or more of the third, fourth, and/or sixth cranial nerves
Granulomatous inflammation of the cavernous sinus, superior orbital fissure, or orbit demonstrated by MRI or biopsy
Exclusion of other causes such as neoplasm, infection, or vasculitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of unilateral orbital pain, cranial nerve III/IV/VI palsy, imaging evidence of granulomatous inflammation, and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging and response to steroids; biopsy is rarely performed.

pathognomonic.notes: Severe, persistent orbital pain preceding cranial nerve palsies
searchTerms: pain near eye on one side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ophthalmoplegia due to cranial nerve III palsy
pathognomonic.notes: Partial or complete paralysis of oculomotor nerve

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ophthalmoplegia due to cranial nerve VI palsy
pathognomonic.notes: Abducens nerve palsy causing lateral rectus muscle weakness

common.notes: Drooping of the upper eyelid due to oculomotor nerve involvement
Double vision from extraocular muscle palsy
Trochlear nerve involvement causing vertical diplopia
Forward displacement of the eye due to orbital inflammation
Redness of the conjunctiva from inflammation

occasional.symptomName: Sensory loss in the distribution of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve (V1)
occasional.notes: Hypoesthesia or numbness in the forehead and upper eyelid
searchTerms: sensory loss in upper trigeminal nerve area

occasional.notes: Ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis due to sympathetic chain involvement
Pain in areas innervated by trigeminal nerve branches
Decreased vision due to optic nerve involvement or orbital inflammation

rare.notes: Optic nerve dysfunction causing vision loss
Trigeminal nerve motor or sensory deficits

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
Normal routine blood tests excluding infection or malignancy
imaging: MRI showing enhancing granulomatous inflammation in cavernous sinus, superior orbital fissure, or orbital apex
Possible enlargement of cavernous sinus or orbital soft tissue swelling
other: Rapid clinical improvement with corticosteroid therapy
Biopsy rarely performed but shows nonspecific granulomatous inflammation

distinguishingFeatures: Fever and systemic signs of infection

redFlags: Signs of systemic infection or sepsis
references: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome: Clinical Features and Management, UpToDate, 2024
